result.summary:
Short answer: mostly yes. I read all 142 numbered lessons and the 25 trap lines in project-notes/Lessons.md, and all 24 numbered lessons and 24 trap lines in film-kit/05 Lessons and traps.md. I checked each one against the plugin (README, every skill and reference file, the 8 agents, the 6 workflows, the hook, kit/docs, the place kit, calculators and film-settings.json). I changed no file. Other helpers were editing the plugin while I read, so line numbers are as of about 03:00 UTC on 23 Oct.

Count of the 142 numbered lessons:
- About 100 are fully carried.
- 14 are partly carried: 40, 41, 42, 70, 72, 73, 80, 81, 82, 83, 84, 94, 120 and 140.
- 14 are missing. Six of those (2, 3, 7, 8, 9, 10) are about the anidoodle drawing tool, which no place uses. The other eight are 13, 35, 36, 37, 38, 39, 141 and 142.
- 14 are about narration, sound or research. I skipped them as instructed, but they are carried too (tips guide sections 2, 3 and 15).
- Of the 25 Lessons.md trap lines, 18 are carried, 1 is partly carried (the free-disk trap), 5 are missing and 1 is research.
- The 24 numbered lessons in film-kit 05 are all in the plugin copy. Its 13-line wet-lockout block is missing.

Most of the lessons that matter for building a new place are carried in layers: a short rule in the tips guide (kit/docs/LLM tips and tricks.md), a step in a skill, and usually a tool with a test. These cover composing a shot, the camera slide, the painter's traps, people, smoke, lettering, light, model measuring, money and filming limits.

Five things are not carried well:
1. The newest lessons (21 Oct, logs 37 and 38) are absent. The plugin kit was last synced on 16 Oct (kit/kit-sync-notes.md:7).
   - The dark and wet street lessons are missing. kit/paper-film/stage/cinema-stage.js has no look.toe, which the source stage has, so a model cannot even apply the fix.
   - The lockout-test.js scene still uses vignette 0.3.
   - Lessons 141 and 142 are missing, and 140 is only partly carried.
2. A cluster of lessons from the paper house sample (36 to 42, 81, 82, 84) appears only as code comments in kit/paper-film/scenes/house-sample/house-set.js, or as bare headings in an inventory list at kit/calculators/README.md lines 238 to 257. That list claims 401 of 423 hand-found items are now worked out by tools. I checked several headings against the tool each is filed under and found no matching code.
   - 'Folded props shading themselves dark' is filed under plan_lights.py.
   - 'Letters that change into other letters in cut-out fonts' is filed under view_audit.py.
   - 'Drawing time comes from surfaces, not shapes' is filed under plan_budget.py.
   - 'Hero props need full detail' is filed under model_lint.py.
   - 'Rebuild from a fresh copy' is filed under preflight.py.
   Treat the inventory as a to-do list, not as proof of coverage.
3. Two helper workflows carry less than the lessons say. workflows/critique-film.js has no dedicated history critic and does not pass the 'what critics must still judge' list from the tips guide section 19. Its picture critics are also told 'right 140 px', the older rule, where rule 12 is 0.90 across. workflows/verify-facts.js is given only the script and on-screen words, never the pictures (lessons 83 and 94).
4. The prompt-time hook (hooks/place-reminder.py) points only at the surface-and-wear skill. The composing, painting and camera lessons reach a model only if it then opens build-and-paint-a-place or the tips guide. That is what its description and the master skill tell it to do, but nothing forces it.
5. Smaller gaps: the lesson 72 advice (check whether a repository is public; when a safety check blocks a save, remove what it objects to and ask, don't force it), the lesson 73 fresh-copy rebuild, and the lesson 120 Blender 5.2 light-linking quirk (carried only in code).

Not tested: I did not run any tool or a model against the plugin. 'Covered' means the rule is written down and quotable, not that a smaller model follows it.

lessons.lesson: L13 and trap: cut-out lettering can turn one letter into another (a T read as I, a narrow I as a slash). Check every title letter by letter at full size and keep those letters out of those fonts.

lessons.lesson: L57, L58 and trap: a camera that never stops reads restless on a phone. Holds still, at most three named moves a shot (built into the engine), and camera moves are measured against the thing in focus, not the aim point.

lessons.lesson: L60, L62, L67 (setup part): Blender's MCP server works headless; Blender's renderer is too slow to film with (35-90 s a frame), so Blender builds models and the stage films them; Blender adds '.glb' to a file name that lacks it; its sandbox refuses read_factory_settings (use read_homefile(use_empty=True, use_factory_startup=True)); the default renderer crashes without a card (set Cycles first); the add-on needs --online-mode.

lessons.lesson: L67 (modelling part): bevels shaded as hard facets because harden_normals was off, and cut brick walls had razor corners; fix with harden normals plus weighted normals, bevel after cutting, and join parts by material (232 parts to 19).
lessons.plugin_evidence: skills/make-3d-models/blender-mcp-notes.md:412 'bevel 0.010 to 0.012 with harden_normals=True, smooth shading, then weighted normals', :528 (bevel after the cut), :389-392 (join parts that share a material); skills/make-3d-models/SKILL.md:70-72; the place kit's surfaces step bevels with hardened normals.
lessons.why: This is the most visible quality difference in a Blender model, and the plugin carries it both as text and in the code.

lessons.lesson: L61: baking corner shading: keep it local and small (reach 0.6, 1024 px, 32 samples, 2 minutes); a part left out of the bake must not share a material with a baked part or it turns dark brown.
lessons.plugin_evidence: skills/make-3d-models/SKILL.md:111-113 'Baked shading ... 1024 px, 32 samples, reach 0.6 units, about 2 minutes ... A part left out of the bake gets its own material copies automatically.'

lessons.lesson: L65: corner checks miss a flat card's middle; the clearance check samples points across every face, and the overlap check ignores hidden parts.
lessons.plugin_evidence: kit/paper-film/scenes/cinema-kit.js:198-218 (room.clearance samples up to 600 points); skills/build-cinema-page/camera-and-framing.md:132-144 (nothing passes through anything).

lessons.lesson: L66: words over a busy set need a soft dark band behind them.
lessons.plugin_evidence: kit/docs/LLM tips and tricks.md:471-472 (topShade; view_audit.py title-contrast); skills/build-cinema-page/guide.md:183-186 and :159-160.
lessons.why: Readability of on-screen words over a place's busy background.

lessons.lesson: L68: a detail can read as something else on a phone (stone blocks beside round gutter ends read as little cameras, glass lenses as sunglasses, a wood pattern as a contour map); a before-and-after judge in the real film frame caught all three.
lessons.plugin_evidence: kit/docs/LLM tips and tricks.md:602-603 and :638-639 'Look at stills at phone size (about 300 px wide) and ask what else could this read as'; skills/check-and-critique/SKILL.md:28; kit/paper-film/blender/build_factory.py:353, :366 (the fixes, as comments).

result.summary:
I went through Decisions.md (items 1 to 44 and its Traps), Workflows.md, Glossary.md and the sets, places and props parts of Status.md line by line, and checked each lesson against the plugin as it stood on 23 October, about 03:00. Other helpers were editing it while I read, for example a new place_kit/variations folder appeared. I did not change any file. I skipped lessons that are only about narration, research, fact-checking or sound, and the Glossary's austerity terms, which are research.

I recorded 94 lessons. About 53 are covered, about 23 are partly covered and about 18 are missing. The big, repeated user rules are well covered and mostly enforced by tools or preflight stages: the camera rule, no clipping, phone safe areas, no real portraits, own lettering, composition and the shot checker, painter words and line-up, fresh checkers, the money rules, and Cycles when lights are on.

The gaps cluster in the newest work, logs 37 to 44, and in how the person works:
- **Dark and wet painted places.** The stage's colour curve darkens dark painted values (the wet road arrived at 0.75 to 0.86 of its painted brightness). The plugin's cinema-stage.js has no `toe` value and no document mentions the fix or the 'arrives at X of painted' measure. The rule that wet and dry paintings go in as a pair is not written either.
- **Checking after a change.** Nothing says to draw a scene at least three times before calling a difference real, or to run a control before blaming a cause.
- **Cycles caveats.** Cycles in moving pictures, and the painter working from Cycles plates, are untested, but nothing in the plugin says so.
- **Limits of the method.** Nothing says a painted plate cannot give a camera moving through the street or light that reacts to characters.
- **Working habits.** Missing: start with one small test and wait for the person's reaction, offer alternatives for a look, keep what the person approved beside any new version, 'a test stays a test', check Decisions.md before a change, save to the repository after each piece of work, and what to do at 'wrap up'.
- **Props.** The no-blank-signs rule sits in one skill, while paint-and-cut says to ask the painter for blank placards, and make-3d-models does not carry it.
- **Rejected house sample.** The person rejected it, but it ships as a worked example with no warning.

The README itself says it was not tested that a smaller model, given only a plain place request, loads the skill by itself. So covered here means written down, not proven to be followed.

Scope note: this story file has no log on the coal mine, the texture and weathering work, the Japanese garden or the rented card. The place logs it does contain are 15 to 16, 19 to 32 and 34 to 39. Mine, textures and garden lessons will come from the other source groups.

I listed 119 lessons. Counting my own judgements, 81 are covered, 25 are partly covered and 13 are missing. The plugin carries the bulk of what the story learned about composing a shot, the camera, lights, people, the painter's habits, lining up paintings, behind paintings, Blender model quality, fresh critics and money. Most of it sits in four places: the tips guide (TIPS), 07 Composing a shot, the place skill (BPP), and calculators that read KS, a table of house numbers with sources. The README (L124-131) says plainly that no outside model has yet used the plugin alone.

The gaps that matter most for a model building a new place, in order:
1. The wet lockout work of log 37 never reached the plugin. The plugin's stage (kit/paper-film/stage/cinema-stage.js) has no `toe` setting, so dark wet or night roads arrive about 25% darker than painted. The film kit's copy has `toe` at lines 216-267.
2. Nothing teaches how to prove that a change to shared code leaves other scenes unchanged (lessons 141 and 142). Only two bare numbers in KS carry it, and one of them (`checking.kept_shot_changed_pixels` = 0) would mislead. The calculators README (L229) says regression stills are not in the preflight.
3. No step has a fresh helper judge the filmed clip in motion. Three separate logs (27, 29, 32) found faults that stills could not show.
4. There is no history or period critic slot in any workflow, and the lettering on 3D props is outside the fact-check workflow.
5. Invented names (newspaper mastheads, firms) are never checked against real ones.
6. The README (L245-ish inventory) claims view_audit.py tells two similar buildings apart. The code does not do it.
7. The older paint-and-cut instruction 'the lower quarter of the picture is the empty floor' is still live (paint-and-cut L35, 04 Painting prompts L17, 02 L46). Log 26 traced the empty bottom of the frame to this rule.
8. The Works and checkout Blender builders are not in the plugin. The kit-sync-notes say they are waiting for a later copy.
9. Smaller items: a shell dollar-sign trap that silently damages price files, a banding check for dark skies, keeping old assets with a note on how to go back, and the lesson that round 6 was stopped with untested changes.

Two places where the README claims more than the code shows: the view_audit claim in item 6, and the 'regression stills' step, which is described but not built.

lessons.lesson: In a built-and-painted set the camera never turns during a move: slide it in a straight line toward the subject, one slide per shot, from one spoken word to another, gentle start and stop, and stop on the composed frame. A turn slides where the street's lines meet and the plate is only slightly wider than the film frame.
lessons.plugin_evidence: 07 rule 11 (L125-134: 'Move the camera without turning it. Slide it in a straight line toward the subject...'); skills/build-cinema-page/camera-and-framing.md section 1a (L66-84); TIPS L208-209 'Never close a gap by turning'; paper-film/tools/camera_audit.py --built-set checks it.
lessons.why: This was the fault the person felt ('camera movement a little odd'); a model that pans or pushes in tears the painting and breaks the composition.

lessons.lesson: Turn the camera once to put where the street's lines meet beside the subject, then only slide. A turn cannot close the gap between the meeting point and the subject because it moves both together; slide or move the subject.
lessons.plugin_evidence: 07 rule 1 (L52-61); TIPS L208-209 and trap 7 (L583-584); calculators/plan_shot.py plans it and camera_audit.py --built-set checks it.
lessons.why: Fixing a gap by turning is the natural wrong move and it was made at least twice.

lessons.lesson: The main composing rule: every strong thing (where the lines meet, the brightest parts, the biggest near props, the warm light, the story props) points at the same corner. Fix the one that points elsewhere first.
lessons.plugin_evidence: 07 'The main rule' (L25-48); TIPS L223-224; the shot checker's rules 1, 5 and 6 (paper-film/tools/check_shot.py).
lessons.why: It is the measured reason one frame looked arranged and the other did not; the user called it 'hard to vary'.

lessons.lesson: Even weight left and right does not make a picture look arranged: the unarranged clip was just as even (46:54) as the liked picture (43:57).
lessons.plugin_evidence: 07 L40-45 and rule 10 (L119-123: 'it does not make the shot work on its own').
lessons.why: Stops a model from balancing weight and calling the shot done.

lessons.lesson: Stand the camera where a person would stand to look at the subject: standing eye height, level (not tipped or leaning), on the pavement not in the middle of an empty road.
lessons.plugin_evidence: 07 rule 2 (L63-69); TIPS L204-206; KS camera.eye_height_range_metres 1.5-1.9, default 1.7; plan_shot.py.
lessons.why: Camera placement decides every later number; a middle-of-the-road camera was one of the three reasons the lockout clip failed.

lessons.lesson: When the person likes a picture, match its camera by landmarks (wheel hubs, chimney top, gate, roofline, kerbs) before moving any prop. Our camera had been 0.42 m too high and 1 degree under-turned; the lines in a painting never meet at one exact point.
lessons.plugin_evidence: TIPS L241-242 ('match its camera by landmarks before moving any prop'); KS camera.reference_landmarks_minimum 5; 07 L60-61 (trace by hand when under 15 lines). The solver paper-film/blender/solve_shot.py is listed as not built (calculators/README.md L230).
lessons.why: A model told 'make it like this picture' will otherwise move props around a wrong camera.

lessons.lesson: Build the story props as one touching group (chair against the board, lantern on the seat, pail at the chair's feet): props that touch read as a sentence, props apart on bare cobbles read as a list.
lessons.plugin_evidence: 07 rule 3 (L71-78) and rule 9 (L114-118); TIPS L226-229; the checker's group-in-a-box test.
lessons.why: Gives a place a story without people.

lessons.lesson: Overlap clearly or leave a clear gap: never let two edges at different distances just touch. Measure the longest stretch where edges run along each other (a post 2 px behind a drum for 113 px) and check background props too.
lessons.plugin_evidence: 07 rule 4 (L80-85) and 'What it knows' (L189-197); TIPS L226-229 (about 15 px overlap or 18 px gap; background props in pairs_also); make_check_file.py.
lessons.why: Near-touches survived three rounds of critics until a tool measured them.

lessons.lesson: The subject must be the biggest bright thing and the sky dim: notice 3.1 times the frame mean and about 60% of the brightest parts; a white chair is dirtied so it stays darker than the notice; a lit lantern's flame may outshine the subject but not its glass.
lessons.plugin_evidence: 07 rule 5 (L87-92) and L198-201; TIPS table L96 (at least 1.8 times the mean) and 7.7; plan_lights.py.
lessons.why: Without it the eye lands on the sky or the fire instead of the story.

lessons.lesson: Light the subject from the people's own lights, from below, with a narrow key linked to it alone; cut a light's reach before its strength; fire 900 to 160 W and lantern 60 to 5 W cured 'everything near white'; the fire's light must skip the drum and chair, the lantern's skip the lantern.
lessons.plugin_evidence: 07 rule 6 and 'Which lights reach which props' (L94-98, L202-205); TIPS 7.1-7.3 (L305-312), 7.8 and trap 6 (L323-325, L580-582); plan_lights.py; set_dressing.light_reaches.
lessons.why: Light linking and starting watts replaced 26 rounds of lighting by eye.

lessons.lesson: Use the height of the tall frame: the nearest story thing must reach 0.70 down; bare paving in the bottom third means the camera stands too far back (camera moved 1.2 to 3 m nearer).
lessons.plugin_evidence: TIPS L211-213 and trap 2 (L569-573); 07 rule 7 and the checker's story_reaches_down (07 L220-226); plan_shot.py and frame_geometry.py reach.
lessons.why: Every Works view passed the main rule yet left the bottom third empty.

lessons.lesson: Sort props by meaning: story props near, big, warm, lit; work props small, far, dim and in the middle band; nothing big and dark in the bottom-left where the eye enters (the sacks covered about 7% there).
lessons.plugin_evidence: 07 rule 8 (L107-112); TIPS L229-230; the checker's rule 8.
lessons.why: A cheap way to stop a street feeling like a catalogue.

lessons.lesson: Keep what must be read left of 0.90 across; clear the phone-button strip by sliding the camera a few centimetres (0.14 m), never by turning.
lessons.plugin_evidence: 07 rule 12 (L136-140); TIPS L99 and L221-222; frame_geometry.py boxes; plan_shot.py.
lessons.why: Content under the app buttons is lost on a phone.

lessons.lesson: Several plausible reasons for why the liked picture works were thrown out as untrue of almost any picture or unsupported: thirds, 'cool blue makes orange strong', 'subject on the right because we read left to right' (the mirror image still works), 'three flames make a triangle'.
lessons.plugin_evidence: Only the thirds reason is carried: TIPS L243 'A rule-of-thirds reason was tested and dropped (log 30). Don't use it.' The other three rejected reasons appear nowhere (grep for 'mirror image', 'triangle', 'cool blue').
lessons.why: A model asked 'why does this composition work' would offer the discarded reasons again.

lessons.lesson: A prop standing on the ground cannot be raised on screen: it rises as it moves further away. The checker turns 'higher/lower' into 'further/nearer', and fixes are in metres (pail 0.25 m right got 'move 0.25 m left'; drum sunk 0.30 m got 'raise 0.30 m').
lessons.plugin_evidence: 07 L185-187 ('A prop standing on the ground can't be raised on screen...'); check_shot.py.
lessons.why: Makes the tool's advice usable by a model that thinks in screen space.

lessons.lesson: Check a Blender shot with measurements from the 3D scene itself (every prop drawn in its own flat colour, camera, meeting point, lights, distance, size, what each stands on), not with a line finder run on a picture.
lessons.plugin_evidence: 07 'Checking a shot automatically' (L142-175); TIPS L69-71 (trust the 3D facts over a line finder); paper-film/blender/shot_facts.py; check-shot.sh.
lessons.why: Exact facts removed guesswork; the line finder found only 47 of the lines and needs about 15 crisp ones.

lessons.lesson: Test a new checking tool by planting faults on purpose (eleven ways, each named first, the report's first fix must name it) and by having independent helpers try to break it (one follows its reports, one plants new faults, one reads the code, one reads the reports as the person would, a skeptic checks their findings).
lessons.plugin_evidence: 07 L214-222; paper-film/blender/tests/break_scene.py and run-checker-tests.sh; BPP L176-180; calculators/README.md L225-227 (hold-out cases). The planted-fault run is still by hand (calculators/README.md L229).
lessons.why: The method that made the checker trustworthy; useful for any tool a model builds.

lessons.lesson: Advice must be followed to be tested: putting the lantern back on its chair as the checker said dropped it to the pavement.
lessons.plugin_evidence: TIPS L65-66 (item 6: 'Test a tool's advice by following it once ... lesson 108').
lessons.why: Stops a model from trusting a report's fix without measuring again.

lessons.lesson: Every report says which version of the tool made it, and files must not change while helpers check them, or two helpers check different things.
lessons.plugin_evidence: 07 L212; TIPS L78-79 (item 11); calculators/README.md L55-56 (inputs hashed, tools versioned, a changed input makes the report STALE).
lessons.why: Keeps parallel checking honest.

lessons.lesson: A hard black wedge across the road was not lighting but a render fault: Blender ran out of shadow memory ('Shadow buffer full' in its log). Read the render log before judging any light; the checker now reads it.
lessons.plugin_evidence: TIPS L67-68 (item 7) and trap L591; 07 L205-207; calculators/plan_lights.py render-log; KS light.render_faults and light.shadow_pool_size 1024; BPP L188-189.
lessons.why: A picture drawn with the fault cannot be judged and costs a paid repaint if sent.

lessons.lesson: Remove or thicken thin parts the painter would smear (the pail's thin wire handle was removed; posts cut level with the board).
lessons.plugin_evidence: TIPS L396-397 (item 9.4: wires, rungs and bars under 6 px); KS painting.plate_thin_parts_pixels_at_1080 = 6; paint_request.py preflight 'thin parts'.
lessons.why: Paid repaints garble thin things.

lessons.lesson: Keep the quiet side of the frame dim and finely detailed, not a black empty mass: a soft cool light on the left houses at about 0.6 of the sky's brightness, sacks and dustbins moved into view, one dim lit window.
lessons.plugin_evidence: 07 rule 10 (L119-123); shot-kind profiles in KS (shot_kind_profiles); TIPS 7.
lessons.why: A black left half made the frame lopsided even when the main rule passed.

lessons.lesson: When the whole frame is a third darker than the reference, raise the dusk sky (1.4 to 1.96) and set each view's exposure from its measured brightness on the painting.
lessons.plugin_evidence: TIPS L328-329 (item 7.10: set exposure from the painting's brightness) and KS light.exposure_range 1.0-1.8; rule 5 (07 L87-92) says 'Dim the sky'. The reason to raise the sky when the frame is too dark is not stated; place_light starting values are 'a first try, not tuned'.
lessons.why: Two rules (dim sky, bright enough frame) pull against each other and the plugin gives no tie-break.

lessons.lesson: Measure a model before fitting anything to it. A sooty lining sized from a helper's guess (0.365 m radius in a 0.296 m drum) stuck out as an orange band and brought the drum's edge within 9 px of the notice.
lessons.plugin_evidence: TIPS L335-336 (item 8.1: 'never use a size worked out from a helper's picture (lesson 116)'); model_lint.py --index; skills/make-3d-models/SKILL.md (measure before fitting).
lessons.why: A suggested fix from a skeptic made a new fault until measured.

lessons.lesson: Record each model's front direction once: the chair's back faced the fire and hid the lantern.
lessons.plugin_evidence: TIPS L338-340 (item 8.3: 'Record each model's front direction once. Check: model_lint.py (names, fronts; --write-index)').
lessons.why: Imported props face unknown ways.

lessons.lesson: A pure-black opening reads as open to the painter: the shut colliery gates were lost in a black doorway; put dim shut doors behind them.
lessons.plugin_evidence: TIPS L394-395 (item 9.3: 'No pure-black openings'); paint_request.py preflight black holes.
lessons.why: A painted gate came back open.

lessons.lesson: Imported glass keeps its see-through value from its picture, which makes lamps and lanterns flat amber cards; unhook it so the mantle and flame show. A lamp's glass may not outshine its flame.
lessons.plugin_evidence: TIPS L344 (item 8.6) and L315-317 (7.5); model_lint.py glass check.
lessons.why: A frequent look-alike fault that survived two rounds.

lessons.lesson: After moving the camera, refresh the scene before any code that reads it: the picker for lit windows used the old camera and put the extra window off frame.
lessons.plugin_evidence: TIPS L337 only says cast placement rays 'after view_layer.update()'; the calculators/README.md inventory line (L256) names 'Refreshing the Blender scene after moving the camera'; code calls view_layer.update() (assemble_notice_corner.py L114). No skill states the rule for camera changes.
lessons.why: Silent, and only a critic noticed the missing window.

lessons.lesson: A kerb or gutter must not read as steps, and its shadow must not join the drum's shadow into one dark pool where the eye enters: use a plain stone colour sitting just under the road (a pale stripe and a joined pool were tried and failed).
lessons.plugin_evidence: grep for gutter, kerb, steps in skills, docs, README: only unrelated hits (gutters as wear places, the notice corner's accepted gutter in place_facts.py L476). 07 rule 8 (nothing big and dark bottom-left) covers the principle only.
lessons.why: Street edges are in every street; but the cure is tied to one scene.

lessons.lesson: Painting the near props out takes their shadows away: keep the main painting everywhere except inside the props' own outlines, and carry the shadows' darkening into the narrow gap kept round each prop, or a pale outline 10 to 15 px wide appears round the prop.
lessons.plugin_evidence: TIPS L412-413 (10.2) and trap 4 (L576-578); BPP L231-237; after_painting.py check --behind; keep_painted_shadows.py; KS painting.keep_painted_shadows_widen_pixels 10 (source 'lessons 122, 125').
lessons.why: This was the one fault a viewer would see in the finished clip, and the first fix made a new one.

lessons.lesson: Tell the painter to keep every shape and light and dark, and never add flames, smoke, glows or new shadows round the near props (they would slide or blink out when the camera moves); leave flames out of the plate and draw them live; describe each story prop's state (dull rust drum, dark sooty mouth, shut gates against grey doors).
lessons.plugin_evidence: 05 L105 ('Leave flames out of the plate ... draw them live'); TIPS L398-402 (9.5-9.6); kit/calculators/templates/paint-prompt.txt; paint_request.py prompt.
lessons.why: The painter adds things nobody asked for; the film draws them live.

lessons.lesson: All lettering is ours, on its own surface: the painter garbles small print (the notice and colliery sign came back as blurred marks), so the notice keeps its own sharp copy.
lessons.plugin_evidence: TIPS L287-288 (item 6.1); 05 L104; BPP L87-89 and L252 (ownSurface); projected-set.js ownSurface.
lessons.why: The close shot has to read the notice.

lessons.lesson: The painter shifts and stretches its picture (0.65% and 3 px): line every painting up with its plate before anything else (96% of outlines on painted edges against 70%).
lessons.plugin_evidence: TIPS L410-411 (10.1); skills/paint-and-cut/SKILL.md section 5.3; align_painting.py; after_painting.py check; KS painting.align_results.
lessons.why: Everything projected back onto the set depends on this.

lessons.lesson: Give near props a 'behind' painting (the same painting with the props painted out) because the painter's outlines round props lie on the road and show as pale or dark ghosts when the camera moves; and a helper pass over the whole frame must not test depth, or leftover depth silently throws half of it away.
lessons.plugin_evidence: 05 L101-103 and L108-110; BPP L231-237 and trap L309 (runPass); TIPS L412-413; after_painting.py --behind; make_behind_picture.py.
lessons.why: The ghost outlines were the biggest fault of the first built-and-painted clip.

lessons.lesson: Hand over from the painting to the behind painting before the eye can see the gap, as soon as the camera starts to move (it first waited for too much movement and took three tries to find).
lessons.plugin_evidence: Carried in code only: projected-set.js L446-449 ('the painting gives way to the behind painting as soon as the camera moves') and KS painting.projected_set.quickMove. No skill or tip states it as advice (grep for 'hand over', 'handover').
lessons.why: A model rewriting the projection would not know the timing matters.

lessons.lesson: Give each near prop a soft 3D contact shadow, faded in as the camera starts to move; a barrel's painted scorch ring faded away and the barrel seemed to float.
lessons.plugin_evidence: TIPS L447-448 (12.4); BPP L253-255; plan_effects.py contact-shadows; KS effects.contact_shadow.
lessons.why: Painted shadows vanish on a move.

lessons.lesson: Painted clouds need somewhere to land: put the painted sky alone on a far card, or a strip of sky behind a tower shows as a pale double edge.
lessons.plugin_evidence: 05 L106-107; BPP L248 (skyCard); projected-set.js skyCard; KS painting.sky_card.
lessons.why: A visible seam in every moving shot of a street.

lessons.lesson: Keep joints, tacks and stains clear of letters (a rust stain hid the A, a tack punched a hole in the E).
lessons.plugin_evidence: TIPS L298-299 (6.6); KS lettering.plank_joint_clear_metres 0.03.
lessons.why: Cheap to avoid, only seen at full size.

lessons.lesson: Seat every prop on the first surface a ray from above meets and check what each stands on: the notice board floated in mid-air (posts landed on top of it and at the street's start).
lessons.plugin_evidence: TIPS L337 (8.2) and L235-237; BPP L158-161 (place_prop); the construction check in skills/surfaces-wear-and-construction (every part carried).
lessons.why: Floating props were caught only by critics before.

lessons.lesson: Flames lit by the fire's own lamp render as white paper cones; flames of three ragged shapes in different sizes and leans, drifting smoke (not a stiff sheet) and a calmer glow pulse (2.8% swing slid the glow's rim on the road, 1.2% did not) read right.
lessons.plugin_evidence: TIPS L446 (12.3 vary flames) and L315-317; 07 L202-205 (light linking); plan_effects.py fire; KS effects.glow_size_swing_share 0.012 and effects_planner.flame_variety_min.
lessons.why: Fire is the one live effect in the street and looked wrong twice.

lessons.lesson: Props must be higher quality than plain boxes: no blank signs, book covers or plain boxes; every sign carries real lettering, built by script when Poly Haven has none.
lessons.plugin_evidence: BPP L85-89 ('No blank signs, book covers or plain boxes: every sign carries real lettering'); surfaces-wear-and-construction skill (the finishing pass on every prop).
lessons.why: The person's explicit instruction.

lessons.lesson: Text on a 3D prop is a claim: the notice's wording was matched to a real 1926 colliery letter and its dates checked (30 April 1926 was a Friday, 1 May a Saturday); a history helper found the subsidy link.
lessons.plugin_evidence: skills/check-facts/SKILL.md and workflows/verify-facts.js check the script and page files (onScreen=page-*.js), not lettering written inside Blender prop scripts (build_scripted_props.py L708 holds the notice text). TIPS L605-606 asks a history critic to check every painted object, but names no step for prop lettering or weekday/date checks.
lessons.why: Wrong dates on a prop notice would pass every tool.

lessons.lesson: Invented names on props (a newspaper masthead, a firm) must be checked against real ones: THE EVENING LAMP was checked against 1,617 New Zealand newspaper titles; the colliery and firm names were deliberately invented.
lessons.plugin_evidence: grep for 1,617, masthead, newspaper title, real title, real brand, invented name across skills, docs, kit: nothing. paint_request.py --real-names guards real people only.
lessons.why: A made-up shop or paper name can accidentally copy a real one, which the film must avoid.

lessons.lesson: Use free Poly Haven models and surfaces (any use), and open every downloaded texture at full size to look for stickers, brands and digits; paint out a maker's label.
lessons.plugin_evidence: BPP L78-81 (PAINT_OUT); TIPS L350 (8.10); skills/surfaces-wear-and-construction/surface-recipes.md L134-136; kit/place-kit/SOURCES-AND-LICENCES.md.
lessons.why: Licence-safe and avoids stray brands in a painted film.

lessons.lesson: A history critic must look at every painted object, not only the words: too much coal in a lockout, snow-like blotches on a May road (painter added), sacks shaped like clay jars, wrong-era tanks, an oil-drum brazier more 1984 than 1926.
lessons.plugin_evidence: TIPS L605-606 and skills/check-and-critique/SKILL.md L29-30 list it as a judgement for 'a history critic', but no workflow or agent has that role: critique-film.js picture critics only say 'anachronistic' (L49) and build-a-place has no period checker.
lessons.why: Period errors passed every tool and were found only by a dedicated history helper.

lessons.lesson: After filming, a fresh helper must look at the finished clip in motion (contact sheet at about 2 frames a second, frame-to-frame scan, close-ups): stills cannot show a fading shadow, a floating barrel, a one-frame colour change or a pale outline that appears only after the move starts.
lessons.plugin_evidence: TIPS L62-64 (never trust a single still), find_jumps.py in the finish stage, BPP L281-282 ('look at the film in motion'), skills/film-and-finish/SKILL.md L214-232 (sheet every 2 s). No agent or workflow commissions a fresh helper to judge the filmed clip; critique-film and check-fixes judge stills before filming.
lessons.why: Three separate logs found real faults only this way.

lessons.lesson: A problem the person accepts on purpose (hidden winding ropes, the brazier, the pail in the caption band) goes in an accepted list with reason, who and date, so it is reported as known and fails again only if it grows.
lessons.plugin_evidence: TIPS L238-240 and L44-46; calculators/README.md L51-58; examples/notice-corner/shot-check.json accepted entries.
lessons.why: Stops the same kept problem blocking every run.

lessons.lesson: Use a picture program only as a composition sketch (Nano Banana Pro with its own camera made the picture the person liked; with our camera it spread props like a catalogue; Flux jammed them; Seedance's video redrew the street); its pictures cannot be cut with ours, and its lettering is garbled (1756, 1828, PRIDAY).
lessons.plugin_evidence: 07 L228-234; 05 L120-121; skills/build-cinema-page/guide.md L240-243; TIPS L287-288; KS money.nano_banana_pro_cents and seedance_10_second_draft_cents.
lessons.why: Saves a model from putting program lettering on screen.

lessons.lesson: Flux takes at most ten pictures per request (so the pail was left out), Nano Banana Pro combines up to 14, a Seedance draft is 480 px wide and can be finished at full size within 7 days without being made again.
lessons.plugin_evidence: grep for 'ten pictures', 'at most ten', 'Seedance', 'Nano Banana' in skills and docs: only the price entries in KS money and the composition-sketch note in 07. No input-limit or draft note.
lessons.why: A model sending eleven prop pictures would hit the limit and lose a paid call.

lessons.lesson: A good camera move for a built street is one continuous approach, barely turning, with a long slowdown onto the subject; Seedance's flaws were hip-height eye and jogging pace and the subject appearing from nowhere.
lessons.plugin_evidence: 07 rule 11 (gentle start and stop) and KS camera.slide_seconds_range 2.6-4.1 and audit_travel_limit_share_per_second 0.012 carry the pace; the 'long slowdown' and hip-height lessons are not stated.
lessons.why: A hint for move design; the slide tools already limit speed.

lessons.lesson: A skeptic re-checks every critic claim against the pictures and rejects some (35 re-checked, 11 rejected, for example 'Seedance ends at an angle to the notice').
lessons.plugin_evidence: workflows/critique-film.js 'Verify' phase (L74-80); place-checker.md mode skeptic (L83-90); TIPS L636-637.
lessons.why: Wrong findings cost a builder an hour.

lessons.lesson: When critics disagree on a number (camera height 1.5 m or 1.85 m), a test picture drawn in Blender settles it.
lessons.plugin_evidence: The range 1.5-1.9 and default 1.7 are set (KS camera.eye_height_*), but no text says to settle a critic disagreement by drawing a test picture.
lessons.why: Avoids arguing between helpers.

lessons.lesson: Objects on their own surface (the notice board's wood, coal sacks as smooth pillows) can look like 3D models rather than paintings in close shots, and faint lines from painted posts show beside real ones; they need copies of the plate's lights in the page.
lessons.plugin_evidence: TIPS L330-331 (7.11: signs on their own surfaces need copies of the plate's lights, or they look flat) and MCPN C4 (lumpy sacks). The look-mismatch itself and the faint post lines are not named.
lessons.why: A known soft spot of the own-surface approach.

lessons.lesson: Painted figures belong to the painting; dark figures laid over it read as shadow puppets and holes. Never answer a face that shows with a silhouette: turn the figure away or move it back.
lessons.plugin_evidence: TIPS L261-265 (5.2) and L551-554 (lesson 137); plan_shot.py never offers a silhouette; KS people.silhouettes_allowed false.
lessons.why: The one result of the people test that changes how every crowd is made.

lessons.lesson: Painted men came back much paler than in the plate (about 15% to 50% of their surroundings' brightness) and turned mid-grey on a phone; darken them back and check outlines, count and skin.

lessons.lesson: Tool research: Blender's fast mode runs under a virtual screen at about 20 s a picture; object makers (SAM 3D, TRELLIS 2 cents; Tripo 20-40 cents) make single objects not scenes; never use Tripo's free plan (its terms give Tripo rights to what free users make); world makers (World Labs about US$1.26 a world, US$5 minimum) need uploads.

lessons.why: The licence trap is the one thing worth saying.

lessons.lesson: Stand-ins for near upright parts of a painting: fit to the four painted corners when the painting's perspective is inconsistent, widen the painted-out areas to remove ghosts, show painting with no lamp on both the stand-in and the room, push the painted-out background back, allow edge-on surfaces to wear the painting; a smear still shows on any sideways step.

lessons.lesson: Faults only motion shows in the house sample: crowd rose out of a flat card (cut straight along its bottom and sides: use soft edges behind the kerb), crossfades overlapped like a double exposure (fade one after another), a title lingered through the move, the ceiling and slab sharing a plane flickered.

lessons.lesson: A public repository must hold no soundtrack, no recordings of anyone but the narrator, no keys, and none of other people's work (a book chapter, central bank papers, pages of Blender's manual, another author's animation engine); read every text file in full; sorting by file ending misclassified program files as video; GitHub refuses files over 100 MB.

result.summary:
Short answer to the person's question: yes for most numbers, checks and working rules, no for a set of lighting, world, Blender-trap, painter and helper-discipline lessons. I went through the mine (story, builders' notes, README, code comments), the courtyard story, README and code, the garden add-on test scripts and the garden plan that summarises the add-on rules, and all 31 logs of the procedural-textures story, and checked 134 lessons against the plugin as it is now. Result: 49 covered, 52 partly, 33 missing. Of the 27 high-importance lessons, 22 are covered, 1 partly, 4 missing.

Carried well, and often enforced by gates: the surface-and-wear pass with real normal maps and displacement (normal strength x0.6, relief depths, graded ground mesh, hiding tile repeats); the construction check (carried parts, doorway floor, z-fighting, buried glow boxes, real ray study before rebuilding); fresh checkers that recompute builders' claims (moss 9.8 percent versus 0.6); one fix round; the Cycles-when-lit renderer rule; the rented-card facts (pay-per-second, stale picture, balance stall, estimate is not a bill); money ledgers and live prices; the person's style rule word for word; stage files, owners and frozen ground; the wet-place painter words; wear budgets, joint advice, rubbish masks, 'what shows at film size'; plain-words reporting and the project-story format. The new batching and card-time rules (variations tool, ledger, allowances), written by other helpers while this check ran, cover the garden's US$10.89 card bill; those files were uncommitted and still changing.

Highest-value gaps, all missing: (1) world and light: an all-round backdrop (hills ring, clip end, ground rim hidden), backdrop shapes must not cast shadows or be lit like cloth, low-sun shadow length (the garden's sun 'did nothing'), EEVEE light cut-off and the cold-blue versus warm-gold renderer mood, how to draw light groups into an EXR, 8-bit painted sky and haze; (2) Blender 5.2 traps: geometry-nodes modifier inputs moved to mod.properties.inputs, bulk building instead of per-object loops, hiding groups one at a time to find a mystery mark; (3) helper discipline: a message to a running paid helper woke a second copy and spent US$0.70 (not in the plugin), no thread cap (-t 2) for parallel Blender runs, no safe-opening routine for the person's uploaded code, no general rule against putting the person's email or name in any outside request (only Poly Haven is covered), '$0' damaged by the shell in a spend record, no check that the old version is stable run to run; (4) painted pipeline: behind painting from a props-free twin plate with brightness matched, the free plain sky when the painter adds clouds, the stage 'toe' switch for crushed dark wet roads, concept-image method and which image model kept the style; (5) the person's standing wishes: the immersive moving-camera goal, 'do not use the plugin' must win over the loud REQUIRED header and the hook, the painted-look rules ('No rounded smooth curves. Just edges and flat surfaces that approximate a curve').

Places where the plugin's code differs from what the sources learned: the inside-out check sums one whole object, so one inverted bar in a joined mesh (the 73 headframe parts) can pass; brick walls and slate roofs get normal maps only although the mine displaced them; the wear masks assume a fixed sun (135 degrees) instead of reading the scene's sun lamp; an imported normal map's convention is read from its file name, not measured.

Method notes: I grepped every key word in all plugin md, py, js, json and sh files (excluding test fixtures) before calling anything missing, and read the README, every skill and reference file, agents, the workflow header, hook, tips guide, lessons-and-traps, house rules, place-kit README, DEVIATIONS, SOURCES, data files and the house-numbers table. Line numbers are as of this check. I changed no project file (only a scratch draft in the scratchpad folder) and did not read ~/.runpod or write in japanese-courtyard. Not checked: the contents of the cookbook, kits and street_wet folders beyond what the story says; the outputs of the add-on probe scripts (only their code).

lessons.lesson: A low sun did nothing: a 4 m hall with the sun low behind it throws a shadow about 25 m long over the whole garden, and hazy hills were also blocking the sun; place the sun and remove blocking walls (shadow length is height divided by tan of the sun's elevation).

lessons.lesson: Patterned ground such as raked gravel needs mesh finer than the pattern (at least four mesh squares per line: a 2.5 cm mesh for 12 cm lines), lines about 12 cm apart and 1.5 cm high, rings round rocks; a golden-hour sun 9 degrees up makes a 1 cm ridge throw a 6 cm shadow, and 2.5-3 cm looks ploughed.

lessons.lesson: Hold rocks and stones low and grouped: buried about a third (22 percent before), grouped in threes with different heights, never in a row, none wider at the top than at the base, moss collars at the feet.

merged.answer_for_the_person:
Short answer: yes, mostly. Of roughly 370 separate lessons from the earlier sets (about 490 once you count each reader's list, with many repeats), about 210 are carried in full, about 90 are carried in part, and about 70 are not in the plugin. The 370 and the three totals are my estimate after removing repeats; the per-group numbers the four readers gave are exact. The big, repeated rules you set are well covered, and usually enforced by a tool as well as written down. That covers the tall phone frame, the camera that slides and never turns, no clipping, people, smoke, lettering made by our own code, the painter's habits, lining up paintings, building props in Blender, fresh checkers, money and card time, and Cycles when lights are on.

Important caveat: 'carried' only means the rule is written down and can be quoted. Nobody has tested whether a smaller model, given a plain request for a place, finds and follows it. The README says so itself.

The important gaps:
1. The newest work (21 to 23 October, logs 37 to 39) never reached the plugin. A dark or wet painted road gets crushed by the stage's colour curve. The fix is a setting called toe, and the plugin's stage does not have it, so a model cannot apply the fix.
2. The rule that wet and dry paintings go in and out as a pair is missing, and so is how to prove 'nothing else changed' (draw each picture at least three times first).
3. Routing. The reminder that fires when you ask for a place points only at the surface-and-wear skill. The composing, camera, people and painting lessons reach a model only if it opens a second skill. The multi-helper place workflow defaults to a wide 1200 x 800 frame and carries none of the film-frame lessons.
4. Helper behaviour, not building: never message a helper that is spending money (it woke a second copy and spent US$0.70), never put your email or name in a request to a website, deliver one small test first and wait for your reaction, never overwrite what you approved, and what to do when you are running out of usage.
5. Building the world round a place: an all-round backdrop, hiding the ground's edge, a backdrop that does not block the sun, and low-sun shadow length. These sit in the courtyard and mine logs only.
6. There is no history or period critic in any helper workflow, and the fact-checker is never shown the pictures or the lettering on props.
7. Three places where the plugin contradicts itself and would reproduce a fault already fixed: 'the lower quarter is empty floor' (the cause of empty bottom thirds), 'ask for blank placards' next to 'no blank signs', and the phone-button margin in critique-film.js (140 px, where the current rule is 0.90 across).

Two things I checked and corrected. One reader said the inside-out check in the place kit adds up a whole object, so one flipped bar inside a joined mesh would pass. I read the code and it works per connected piece, so I dropped that claim. And the README's inventory says a tool tells two similar buildings apart; there is no such code, so the inventory is a to-do list in places, not proof of coverage.

I changed no file. I did not read anything in ~/.runpod and wrote nothing in japanese-courtyard. Other helpers were editing the plugin while I read, so line numbers are as of this check.
